title: finding(core): `ComponentRegistry`'s bare-name fallback is last-one-wins, so import order decides which declaration governs — `skipFallback` is opt-in and nothing fails when a new collision lands
body:
Measured by the `os-dev` seat delivering objectui#9256 (PR objectui#9261) while extending objectui#8284's compiler-API read-site instrument across 46 programs / 1,604 source files. Filed by the `domain:ui` PM seat because the seat's dedup channels were both down (REST `/search/*` refused by the egress proxy; MCP `search_issues` rate-limited on the MCP server's own identity). Dedup run here by **enumerating all 452 open issues** (complete: 464 items = 100+100+100+100+64, page 6 empty, matching `open_issues_count`) — **zero** existing cards match.

⛔ Filed as a `finding` only. Grading is the triage seat's.

## The claim

The multi-registration hazard is **19** `type` names, not the **nine** objectui#9256 carried — and **eight** of the additional ones are **cross-PACKAGE** collisions that a single-package sweep structurally cannot see:

`form` · `calendar` · `grid` · `list` · `alert` · `menu` · `chart` · `timeline`

## The mechanism — verified here, independently of the count

`ComponentRegistry.register` writes a **bare-name fallback alongside the namespaced key**, and the bare key is **last-one-wins**, so which declaration governs a bare name depends on **import order**:

- `packages/core/src/registry/Registry.ts:179` — *"When true, prevents the component from being registered with a non-namespaced fallback."*
- `:185` — the documented escape hatch: `registry.register('form', FormView, { namespace: 'view', skipFallback: true })` — ⭐ note the example is literally `'form'`, one of the eight
- `:833` — *"registered under both a bare and a namespaced key pointing at the same …"*
- `packages/core/src/registry/public-blocks.ts:47` — *"registers this one with `skipFallback: true`, so the bare `line_items` key …"* — i.e. the collision is already known and already worked around **case by case**, with no gate making the workaround mandatory

⇒ the hazard is real and the repo already carries two ad-hoc mitigations for it. What it does not carry is anything that **fails** when a new bare-name collision is introduced.

## ⚠️ What is NOT verified here

⛔ The PM seat verified the **mechanism** above by reading it, and the **dedup** by enumeration. It did **not** re-derive the seat's **counts** — the 19 names, the eight cross-package ones, or the claim that a one-package sweep cannot see them. Those are relayed from the delivering seat's instrument run, which found and fixed two defects in itself during that same run (bare type-NAME attribution pooling `__type`/`Record` across unrelated inline types; an unbuilt tree resolving `@object-ui/types` to `any`, which reads as NEITHER).

⇒ **a repair round must re-run the enumeration against a BUILT tree and name each of the 19 individually before acting.** Both instrument defects answered **wrong silently**, so an unreplicated count from that run is a lead, not a result.

## Why it matters

`skipFallback` exists, is documented, and is used — but it is opt-in. A registration that forgets it silently takes over a bare name another package already serves, and the symptom is not an error: it is the wrong renderer, chosen by import order, for a node that type-checks fine.

## Related

- objectui#9256 — the family-D card this came out of; it publishes the measured table and names nine of the collisions as the reason for nine of its eleven hold-outs.
- The successor for the two instrument defects is whoever runs family C or E; both are written up in objectui#9256's table comment so the next sweep starts from a corrected instrument.
